chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Walid ibn Hisham, who said:

I came from Egypt with some slaves, and I passed by the tax collector, so he asked me, and I said: They are all free. Then I arrived in al-Madinah and entered upon Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام and informed him of what I had said to the tax collector.
So he said: There is nothing upon you. I said: Among them is a bondwoman with whom I had relations, and she is pregnant.
He said: No; is not her child the one by whom she is freed? When her master dies, she becomes from the share of her child.

key_terms.أَحْرَارٌ: free persons, as opposed to slaves
key_terms.نَصِيبِ: share or allotted portion in inheritance distribution
key_terms.وَلَدُهَا: her child, whose legal connection affects her status
key_terms.ٱلْعَاشِرِ: the tax collector who questions passing goods or persons

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a pregnant bondwoman who bears her master's child, and does a statement to a tax collector make the slaves free?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal ruling concerning a slave woman who became pregnant by her master and the legal effect of a statement made to a tax collector. Imam Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام rules that no liability attached to the speaker's statement in that case, and clarifies that the mother of his child is connected to the legal status of her child and becomes part of her child's share after the master's death.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3514 - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya, who narrated from al-Walid ibn Hisham:
"I came from Egypt with some slaves, and when I passed by the tax collector (al-'Ashir), he asked me about them. I said: 'They are all free.'
When I arrived in Medina, I went to Abu al-Hasan (as), and informed him about what I had told the tax collector.
Imam (as) said: 'There is nothing upon you.'
I then said: 'Among them is a bondwoman with whom I had relations, and she is pregnant.'
Imam (as) replied: 'Isn't her child the one who will free her? When her master dies, she becomes the share of her child.'"
